## Detailed Findings

#### 1. SST OpenCode saved permission editing MEDIUM (permission, config, ui, api)

- **What**: SST OpenCode PR #56659 (merged 2026-10-19) adds UI and API to edit previously-saved permissions. Commit title: "feat(core): edit saved permissions". Feature: users can modify saved permission rules (allow-patterns, deny-patterns, expiry, scope) after initial save without deleting and re-creating. Use case: typo in glob pattern (saved `src/**/*.ts` but meant `src/**/*.tsx`), broadening scope (saved single-file allow, now want directory allow), narrowing expiry (saved permanent, now want 7-day TTL). Implementation: new `permissions/edit` API endpoint, permission-editor UI in settings panel, validation of edited patterns against existing requests (reject edits that would invalidate prior approvals). Pattern: permissions are immutable after save in most systems; editing avoids re-approval fatigue when fixing mistakes.

- **Why**: Alexi audit 2026-10-19: `src/permission/` contains policy, provenance, drain, prompt, recovery, wildcard, external-directory, config-paths modules. Grep for `edit.*permission|modify.*permission|update.*permission` returned only gating logic (`config-paths.ts` gates `edit` tool permission requests, `drain.ts` never auto-resolves config file edits). No `permissions/edit` endpoint or UI. Feature gap: once a permission is saved in Alexi, user must delete via permission store and re-request, losing audit trail. Editing capability improves UX (fix typos, adjust scope) and preserves provenance (edited rule keeps original timestamp + adds edit timestamp). MEDIUM priority, ~6-8h implementation (add edit API to permission store, update prompt to offer edit action, validate edited patterns, preserve provenance chain, add tests). Scope: CLI-only, no UI panel needed (Alexi is terminal-based), edit action in permission prompt.

- **Source**: https://github.com/sst/opencode/pull/56659 (permission editing upstream), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/permission/ (current modules, no edit capability found)

- **Category**: config

- **Size**: MEDIUM ~6-8h (add edit API to permission store, update permission prompt to offer edit action, validate edited patterns against existing requests, preserve provenance chain with edit timestamp, add unit tests for edit validation and provenance)

#### 2. SST OpenCode provider policy logging SMALL (providers, policy, logging, observability)

- **What**: SST OpenCode PR #56905 (merged 2026-10-19) logs providers removed by policy during catalog refresh. Commit title: "fix(core): log providers removed by policy". Feature: when a provider/model is filtered out by policy rules (e.g. org-wide blocklist, cost cap, compliance constraint), log the removal with policy reason at INFO level. Use case: user reports "model X missing from catalog", admin checks logs and sees "Provider anthropic/opus-4.7 removed by policy: cost-cap-exceeded". Pattern: catalog filtering is opaque without logging, debugging requires code inspection or debug builds. Logging policy removals surfaces filtering decisions for support and audit.

- **Why**: Alexi audit 2026-10-19: `src/providers/modelCatalog.ts` (live catalog refresh + static fallback), `src/providers/health.ts` (provider health checks), `src/providers/capabilities.ts` (capability filtering). No policy-based filtering found (`grep -r "policy.*remov\|filter.*policy" src/providers/` returned zero matches). Current behavior: `modelCatalog.ts` filters by capability (reasoning, vision, streaming) and availability (SAP AI Core deployment status) but does not apply policy rules. Feature gap SMALL: Alexi does not have org-wide policy enforcement yet (no blocklist, cost caps, compliance constraints in config). Pattern is REFERENCE-ONLY unless/until Alexi adds policy-based catalog filtering. If added, remember to log removals with policy reason. SKIP immediate implementation (no policy system exists), REFERENCE for future policy feature.

- **Source**: https://github.com/sst/opencode/pull/56905 (provider policy logging upstream), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/providers/modelCatalog.ts (catalog refresh, no policy filtering found)

- **Category**: providers

- **Size**: SMALL ~2-3h (add policy-based filtering to modelCatalog, log removals with policy reason, add tests) — BUT SKIP until Alexi adds policy enforcement config. REFERENCE-ONLY for now.

#### 3. Cline MCP Resources support ALREADY IMPLEMENTED (mcp, protocol, resources)

- **What**: Cline PR #15165 (merged 2026-10-18) adds MCP Resources protocol support, marked [NO-OP]. Commit title: "Support MCP Resources [NO-OP]". Feature: MCP Resources protocol extension (`resources/list`, `resources/read`, `resources/subscribe`) for servers to expose static data (docs, schemas, reference files) separate from dynamic tools. [NO-OP] tag indicates protocol scaffolding was added (validators, types, client stubs) but no UI/agent consumption yet — servers can advertise resources, client validates, but agent loop does not use them. Pattern: protocol support in two phases (1) scaffolding [NO-OP], (2) agent integration [functionality]. Cline PR is phase 1.

- **Why**: Alexi audit 2026-10-19: `src/mcp/validator.ts` L52-80 validates `resources/list` responses (uri, name, description, mimeType fields), 11 total references to `resources/list|resources/read` across MCP modules. Feature ALREADY IMPLEMENTED at phase-1 scaffolding level (same as Cline [NO-OP] state). Alexi can connect to MCP servers exposing resources, validate responses, but agent loop (`src/core/orchestrator.ts`, `streamingOrchestrator.ts`) does not consume resources for context. SKIP - no gap at current phase. If Cline later adds phase-2 agent integration (e.g. auto-fetch resources matching task, inject into context), re-evaluate.

- **Source**: https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/15165 (MCP Resources [NO-OP] upstream), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/mcp/validator.ts L52-80 (resources/list validation implemented), grep results (11 resource protocol references across MCP modules)

- **Category**: N/A (mcp, protocol, resources, already implemented at [NO-OP] scaffolding level)

- **Size**: SKIP. Alexi MCP Resources support matches Cline [NO-OP] state (validators + stubs, no agent integration). Verified 2026-10-19.

#### 4. Cline terminal keyboard focus REFERENCE-ONLY (vscode, terminal, ide, ui)

- **What**: Cline PR #15061 (merged 2026-10-19) preserves keyboard focus when revealing terminal for command execution. Commit title: "fix(vscode): keep keyboard focus when revealing the terminal for a command". Issue: VS Code extension reveals terminal with `terminal.show(preserveFocus: false)` (default), stealing focus from editor/chat panel every command execution, breaking user flow. Fix: `terminal.show(preserveFocus: true)` so focus stays in chat panel, user can continue typing next prompt while command runs. Pattern: IDE extension ergonomics — terminal reveal for output visibility without disrupting input context.

- **Why**: Alexi is CLI-only with no VS Code extension, JetBrains plugin, or desktop app. Terminal management uses Node.js `child_process` / `execa` in `src/tool/tools/bash.ts` and `shell.ts`, not IDE terminal APIs. REFERENCE-ONLY: if Alexi adds VS Code extension, reference this pattern (use `preserveFocus: true` on terminal reveal, or offer toggle in extension settings). Current priority SKIP - no IDE integration.

- **Source**: https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/15061 (terminal focus preservation upstream), N/A (Alexi is CLI-only, no vscode API)

- **Category**: N/A (vscode, terminal, ide, ui, reference-only)

- **Size**: SKIP. Alexi is CLI-only, no VS Code extension. Pattern reference for future IDE plugin.

#### 5. Cline Gemini native Search disable REFERENCE-ONLY (providers, gemini, tools, native)

- **What**: Cline PR #15194 (merged 2026-10-19) stops sending native Google Search tool on Gemini API. Commit title: "fix(llms): stop sending native Google Search on the Gemini API". Issue: Gemini models (`gemini-2.0`, `gemini-2.5`) have built-in Google Search capability enabled by default when `tools` is omitted or empty in API request. Model invokes search unpredictably (web queries during reasoning, returning search results instead of code), breaking agent loop expectations (agent expects tool calls to be MCP/built-in tools only, not web search). Fix: explicitly send `tools: []` (empty array) instead of omitting field, which disables all native tools including Search. Pattern: Gemini native tools (Search, Code Execution) must be explicitly disabled via empty tools array, not opt-in via tools list.

- **Why**: Alexi audit 2026-10-19: `grep -r "Google.*Search|google.*search" src/providers/` returned zero matches. Alexi does not integrate Google Search tool (native or MCP-based). SAP AI Core model catalog (`src/providers/modelCatalog.ts`) does not expose Gemini models with native tool capabilities (SAP Orchestration proxies Vertex AI Gemini but does not forward native tool schemas). Pattern not applicable to current Alexi setup. REFERENCE-ONLY: if Alexi adds direct Gemini API provider (Vertex AI, Google AI Studio) or SAP exposes Gemini native tools, remember to send `tools: []` explicitly to disable Search/Code Execution when not wanted. Current priority SKIP - no Gemini native tool exposure.

- **Source**: https://github.com/cline/cline/pull/15194 (Gemini Search disable upstream), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/providers/ (no Google Search integration found), SAP AI Core docs (Gemini proxied via Vertex, native tools not exposed)

- **Category**: N/A (providers, gemini, tools, native, reference-only)

- **Size**: SKIP. Alexi does not expose Gemini native tools. Pattern reference for future direct Gemini integration.

#### 6. SST OpenCode session archiving restoration ALREADY IMPLEMENTED (core, session, archive, retention)

- **What**: SST OpenCode PR #53759 (merged 2026-10-19) restores session archiving feature. Commit title: "feat(core): restore session archiving". Feature: two-phase retention lifecycle (archive -> delete). Sessions older than `archiveAfterDays` move to `<sessionsDir>/.archive/` and gzip-compress. Archived sessions older than `deleteAfterDays` (measured from archive file mtime) permanently delete. Archive inspection with `zcat <id>.json.gz | jq`. Pattern: incremental data management (keep recent sessions hot, archive old sessions compressed, delete ancient archives), reduces disk usage while preserving audit trail.

- **Why**: Alexi audit 2026-10-19: `src/core/retentionRunner.ts` (two-phase lifecycle, ARCHIVE_DIRNAME = '.archive', ARCHIVE_SUFFIX = '.json.gz'), `src/core/sessionRetention.ts` (retention policy config), `src/core/retentionScheduler.ts` (cron scheduler), `src/core/scheduledRetention.ts` (scheduled task wrapper). Feature ALREADY IMPLEMENTED with identical pattern (archive to `~/.alexi/sessions/.archive/<id>.json.gz`, delete after `deleteAfterDays`). SKIP - no gap. Verified 2026-10-19.

- **Source**: https://github.com/sst/opencode/pull/53759 (session archiving upstream), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/core/retentionRunner.ts L1-50 (two-phase retention implemented), /home/runner/work/alexi/alexi/src/core/sessionRetention.ts (retention config), ls src/core/ (retentionScheduler.ts, scheduledRetention.ts modules exist)

- **Category**: N/A (core, session, archive, retention, already implemented)

- **Size**: SKIP. Alexi session archiving fully implemented. Verified 2026-10-19.
